evaluation_notes: Synthetic fixture validating the harness, not provider accuracy. Video generated by benchmarks/fixtures/generate.py: 8s white 320x240@15fps with two filled red 50x50 squares at x=20,90 y=95 for the whole clip, plus two more at x=160,230 enabled t=4..8s. Expectation annotated from those generation parameters (verified by pixel count of extracted frames: 5000 red px at t=2, 10000 at t=6), never from a model. sha256 of the author's fixture: 93131e32cc8d6b044ae99a9f43f231cf66b0d398c0cddf742eaee4f63367cfe0 (regenerate locally; videos are gitignored).
instructions: Count the filled red squares visible in the first half of the video (t=0-4s) and in the second half (t=4-8s). Return both counts under counts.squares_first_half and counts.squares_second_half.
known_ambiguities: The count changes at t=4s, so a single sampled frame cannot show both counts; this task defeats the single-frame shortcut that the static objects_counts task cannot.
Counts are reported per half; a square visible for only part of a half would be ambiguous, but by construction each count is constant within its half.
